text: Independent evidence corroborating the 2021 loss includes observations from multiple sources. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13) observed an 81.3-ha tree-cover loss in 2021, which is 2.23% of the asset. The European Commission Joint Research Centre's Global Forest Cover 2020 (JRC GFC2020 V4) data shows that 98% of this event area was mapped as forest in 2020. Additionally, Uruguay's Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries (MGAP) 2021 forest map indicates that the affected area was planted forest, primarily consisting of Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda. These sources collectively confirm the tree-cover loss event in 2021.
